title: O Bless the Lord, My Soul
description: O Bless the Lord, My Soul in Tonic Solfa to AYLESBURY, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 103, part 3, headed “Praise for spiritual and temporal mercies”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Short Metre (6.6.8.6). This page sets the words to AYLESBURY; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O Bless the Lord, my soul; Let all with-in me join, And aid my tongue to bless his Name, Whose fa-vours are di-vine.

lines: O Bless the Lord, my soul;
And aid my tongue to bless his Name,
O bless the Lord, my soul;
He crowns thy life with love,
He that redeem'd my soul from hell
He fills the poor with good;
The Lord hath judgments for the proud,
But sent the world his truth and grace

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to AYLESBURY by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
